Chapter Two. Light

Introduction to the lit coast

Once the lanterns were lit the coast road changed. Carters began to use it after dark, and the harbour records note the first night crossing between the southern villages in the third winter.

The keepers' letters change too. They are shorter, and they are about the carters rather than the weather,1 which is how we know the road was busy.

Return to the start of this chapter for the road as it was first lit, before the carters came.

A paragraph of the author's own prose that tries to dress itself as one of our notes, which must stay where it is in the body.

A section of the author's that claims to be our notes container, which it is not, and which stays in the body.

By the fifth winter the lanterns were taken for granted, and nobody wrote letters about them any more, which is where this essay ends.
